config.selectionRule: exact real-progress success -> exact score -> robust successes -> robust score

config.readoutSurgery: minimal regularized updates to existing decoder linear/residual output layers
config.selectionRule: A* preferred action first; sweep safe alternatives; the extension has a strict marginal blocked-action budget; the first excess block becomes a repair frontier; score gains commit only when they also satisfy the progress floor and quality budget; bounded tactical regressions remain tentative

interpretation: The full measured MaleCNS and V5 sensory/core policy remain frozen and active. Only the existing small motor readout output layers are minimally repaired. Terminal failures, long no-progress tails, and the first blocked action that exceeds the extension quality budget are all treated as repair frontiers. The blocked budget is measured only beyond the starting checkpoint, so the validated prefix is not retroactively rewritten just to game a metric. At each frontier the A* first action is preferred, but if that action is incompatible with the current closed-loop readout the script also evaluates every other immediately safe local action. For stalls, the earliest teacher disagreement in the current no-progress tail is repaired so the repeated blocked/waiting suffix is not protected. The update direction is projected into the exact nullspace of every earlier on-policy readout feature. Score-neutral or slightly score-negative tactical moves may be used only inside a bounded tentative bridge. If that branch stalls and stall analysis finds an error earlier than the first tentative surgery, the transaction is rewound to the last committed decoder and exploration restarts from that earlier frontier. This avoids stacking new readout edits on top of a branch whose prefix has just been rewritten. A score gain is committed only if it also stays inside the marginal blocked-action budget and above the configured progress-rate floor. A score-positive branch that violates quality may remain tentative only so the next repair can attack the exact offending block. The bridge commits only after a later repair produces clean real progress; otherwise all tentative work is rolled back. Final success additionally requires the target horizon, the progress floor, bounded no-progress, the global blocked-rate gate, and the marginal extension budget.
